subject: FinPay - competitive eval & cost/TCO follow-up
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@finpay.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@finpay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: FinPay - competitive eval & cost/TCO follow-up

Hi Sofia / Tom — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

What we heard: 
- Primary use: mixed retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for customer support + analytics, peak concurrency ~60 concurrent users, average response length ~450 tokens, 75% of requests share common prefixes (templates).
- Key buyer concerns: predictable unit economics, caching behavior for repeated prefixes, and latency under concurrency.

How Redwood thinks about the competitive angle (high level):
- Cost: our pricing + runtime optimizations are tuned for production unit economics (batching + KV/prefix caching + quantization options).
- Performance: consistent latency via smart routing and continuous batching; we prioritize tail latency for customer-facing flows.
- Reliability: fallbacks to lower-cost model variants and region routing for capacity resilience.

Attached: redwood_cost_model_v2.xlsx (worked example TCO) and benchmark_results_summary.pdf (high-level throughput/latency comparisons vs hyperscaler endpoints).

Baseline numbers (quick, illustrative):
- Redwood hosted (multi-tenant): $45 per 1M tokens (production average assumptions: avg batch size 6, cache hit 60%, avg seq len 450).
- Redwood dedicated (reserved capacity, quantized): $18 per 1M tokens (higher cache hit & quantization).
- Typical hyperscaler endpoint (public pricing, not optimized for batching/caching) ~ $120+ per 1M tokens for the same model class in our tests.

Notes on assumptions in the attached model:
- Batch assumptions: avg effective batch size = 6 (distribution: 50% single/2, 30% 3-8, 20% >8); batching reduces per-token compute by ~25-35% depending on model.
- Cache assumptions: prefix/KV caching reduces generation token compute by the cache-hit rate; we used 60% in the example.
- Embeddings: embeddings cost modeled separately; for RAG flows we assume embedding refresh cadence and include similarity search infra.

Suggested next tests (we can run both sides):
1) 1M-token synthetic run matching your concurrency profile (we'll run both hosted and dedicated configs).
2) Two-pass: baseline (no cache) and cached (with prefix/KV cache enabled) to measure delta in compute & latency.
3) Real workload sample: you can share a small request set (anonymized) and we run it through our profiler for QoQ metrics.

If this looks good, can we schedule the benchmark window next week? I can loop Marcus (benchmarks/infra) and Lauren (solutions) to coordinate.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
+1 (650) 555-0172

Attachments: redwood_cost_model_v2.xlsx (xlsx, 120KB), benchmark_results_summary.pdf (pdf, 450KB)

From: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@finpay.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@finpay.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 18:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinPay - competitive eval & cost/TCO follow-up

Thanks, Aditya — useful recap. A few clarifying questions before we run anything: 

1) Can you provide a per-1M-token breakdown by model-size class you tested (small, medium, large)? We need line-of-sight for our finance team.
2) Batching assumptions: the spreadsheet references an "avg batch size = 6" — that feels optimistic for our traffic. Can you show sensitivity (avg batch size 2, 4, 8)?
3) Cache hit guidance: you used 60% — our engs think prefix reuse might be closer to 70-80% for support templates. What delta do you see at 70/80%?
4) Does the hosted price you quoted include network and request overheads, or are those line items separate?
5) If we go dedicated, how fast can you provision a pilot environment (1-2 GPUs) and what's the expected uplift to latency and unit cost?

Also, please confirm if embeddings (for vector search) are accounted for separately in the TCO. We'll try to anonymize a 1k-request sample and share it if that helps.

Appreciate it — looking to present a concise number to procurement by next Wed.

— Sofia Ramirez
Head of Product, FinPay
sofia.ramirez@finpay.com

Hi Sofia / Tom — thanks for the questions. Attached is an updated cost model with sensitivity tables (redwood_cost_model_v2.xlsx). Below are the high-level, conservative numbers pulled from that workbook so you can share with procurement quickly. All numbers are per 1,000,000 tokens generated (includes both prompt + completion tokens where noted).

Assumptions common to all rows: avg seq len = 450 tokens; baseline request distribution that yields an effective batch-size distribution as documented in the workbook. Embeddings are modeled separately.

Scenario A — Baseline (no cache, minimal batching):
- Small model class: $135 / 1M tokens
- Medium model class: $230 / 1M tokens
- Large model class: $380 / 1M tokens

Scenario B — Production (hosted, avg batch size ~4, cache hit 60%):
- Small: $60 / 1M tokens
- Medium: $105 / 1M tokens
- Large: $180 / 1M tokens

Scenario C — Optimized (dedicated + quantized + cache hit 75%):
- Small: $22 / 1M tokens
- Medium: $38 / 1M tokens
- Large: $68 / 1M tokens

Key deltas & notes: 
- Batching impact: moving avg batch size from 2 -> 6 reduces per-token compute cost by ~20-30% (sensitivity is in the sheet).
- Cache impact: going from 60% -> 80% hit reduces generation compute proportionally (example: for your template-heavy flows, we often see 40-60% reduction in compute when caching is enabled).
- Hosted price includes request processing, routing, and standard egress but excludes any premium network egress allowances you may have on your side. Embeddings are line-itemed in the sheet (we recommend planning for ~0.5-1M embedding operations per month depending on your vector store refresh cadence).
- Dedicated provisioning: pilot (1x A10-equivalent or similar) can be provisioned in ~5 business days with initial benchmarks in 48–72 hours after access. Dedicated configs yield the "Optimized" numbers when combined with quantized lower-precision models and higher cache hits.

Recommended next steps: 
1) We can run the two benchmark runs you asked for: baseline and cached. Estimated time: 2–4 hours per run, we will provide latency percentiles and token-level cost breakdowns.
2) You share a small anonymized sample (1,000 requests). We'll run it through the profiler and produce a short report with per-endpoint cost, cache hit expectations, and expected savings vs a hyperscaler baseline.
3) If procurement is comfortable, we can provision a 1-GPU dedicated pilot for a 2-week POC to surface real TCO.

Links / files: redwood_cost_model_v2.xlsx (sensitivity tabs), benchmark_results_summary.pdf.

Propose a 30-minute sync to review the workbook Friday 6/12 at 10am PT — does that work for you?

Best,
